item.title: US 'totally' rejects global AI governance at New Delhi summit
item.description:
UN Secretary-General António Guterres used the closing day of the AI Impact Summit in New Delhi on Friday to formally announce that 40 members have been confirmed for the Independent International Scientific Panel on Artificial Intelligence, a body he said would work to "make human control a technical reality — not a slogan."

The declaration came on the final day of the five-day summit — the fourth annual global AI gathering, and the first to be hosted in a developing country — where dozens of heads of state, tech executives, and ministers gathered to debate how to govern a technology advancing faster than the institutions trying to regulate it.

item.title: Gold tops $5,000 as Trump's Iran ultimatum fuels safe-haven rush
item.description: Gold prices pushed above $5,000 an ounce on Friday, propelled by escalating tensions between the United States and Iran and persistent uncertainty over the Federal Reserve's interest rate path. The advance came after President Donald Trump gave Tehran a 10-to-15-day deadline to reach a nuclear deal, warning of "bad things" if diplomacy fails.

item.title: Guterres unveils UN panel to ensure 'human control' of AI
item.description:
UN Secretary-General António Guterres on Friday called for "less hype, less fear" over artificial intelligence as he unveiled the mission of a new international panel of experts, telling leaders gathered in New Delhi that its goal is to "make human control a technical reality — not a slogan."

Speaking at the AI Impact Summit, the first global AI gathering of its scale hosted in a Global South nation, Guterres said the United Nations General Assembly had confirmed the 40 members of the Independent International Scientific Panel on Artificial Intelligence, a body designed to serve as the AI equivalent of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change.

"We are barrelling into the unknown," Guterres said. "That requires meaningful human oversight in every high-stakes decision" and "clear accountability — so responsibility is never outsourced to an algorithm."

item.title: Global stocks trade mixed as AI fears and Iran tensions collide
item.description:
Global markets traded in mixed fashion on Friday as two forces — deepening anxiety over artificial intelligence's disruptive potential and escalating tensions between the United States and Iran — pulled investors in opposite directions.

In Asia, Japan's Nikkei 225 fell 1.1% to close at 56,825.70 as banking and financial stocks slumped, dragged lower by concerns over private lending firms exposed to businesses vulnerable to AI displacement. Hong Kong's Hang Seng slid as trading resumed following the Lunar New Year break, while mainland Chinese markets remained shuttered through next week. South Korea's Kospi bucked the trend, surging 2.2% as defense stocks, led by Hanwha Aerospace, jumped 8.6% on expectations of rising global military spending. In Europe, the pan-European Stoxx 600 edged up 0.2%, approaching an all-time high, while the FTSE 100 gained 0.3% and France's CAC 40 rose 0.5%. U.S. futures pointed to a modestly higher open.

item.title: Old phone batteries and wood pulp waste yield new sodium-ion battery material
item.description:
Researchers have developed a method to convert discarded mobile phone batteries and industrial lignin — two common waste streams — into an advanced electrode material for sodium-ion batteries, offering a potential pathway toward cheaper and more sustainable energy storage.

The study, published on February 10 in the journal Biochar X and announced via EurekAlert on February 18, describes how the team used a hydrothermal process to extract nickel and cobalt compounds from spent phone batteries and combine them with carbon derived from lignin, a natural polymer produced in large volumes by the paper and biofuel industries. The resulting composite material, a nickel cobalt sulfide coated in lignin-derived carbon, demonstrated strong electrochemical performance when tested as an anode in sodium-ion batteries.

item.title: Study links Antarctica's Blood Falls to pressure shifts beneath glacier
item.description: Two studies published in recent months have advanced the understanding of two of Antarctica's most puzzling geological features: the crimson cascade known as Blood Falls and the continent's deep-seated gravitational anomaly, the Antarctic Geoid Low.

item.title: Supreme Court strikes down Trump's sweeping tariffs
item.description:
The U.S. Supreme Court struck down most of President Donald Trump's sweeping global tariffs on Friday, ruling 6-3 that the president exceeded his authority by using the International Emergency Economic Powers Act to impose the duties, according to Bloomberg and NBC News. Justices Kavanaugh, Thomas, and Alito dissented. The decision delivers the most consequential legal defeat of Trump's second term, undercutting the centerpiece of his economic agenda and setting the stage for a complex refund process potentially involving more than $175 billion in tariff revenue collected over the past year.

The ruling arrives in the consolidated cases of Learning Resources v. Trump and Trump v. V.O.S. Selections, Inc., which together tested whether IEEPA — a 1977 law designed for use during national emergencies — authorizes the president to impose broad-based import tariffs without congressional approval. The decision does not affect all of Trump's tariffs, including those on steel, aluminum, and automobiles imposed under separate legal authorities.

item.title: Germany's Merz to visit China next week on first trip as chancellor
item.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz will travel to China next week for his first official visit since taking office in May, seeking what his government described as "the right balance of cooperation" with Europe's largest trading partner amid a rapidly shifting geopolitical landscape.

item.title: UK expects trade with US to hold after Supreme Court strikes down Trump tariffs
item.description:
The British government said Friday that it expects its "privileged trading position" with the United States to endure after the US Supreme Court struck down President Donald Trump's sweeping tariffs in a 6-3 ruling that delivered a rare rebuke to the president's economic agenda.

The decision, authored by Chief Justice John Roberts and joined by Justices Amy Coney Barrett and Neil Gorsuch along with the court's three liberal members, found that the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) "does not empower the President to levy tariffs". But for Britain, officials believe the ruling will have a limited impact on bilateral trade, since the UK's separate deal with Washington — the US-UK Economic Prosperity Deal signed in June 2025 — was largely built on different legal authorities.

item.title: NASA targets March 6 for first crewed moon mission in over 50 years
item.description:
NASA announced Friday that it is targeting March 6 for the launch of Artemis II, the first crewed mission to the vicinity of the moon in more than 50 years, after engineers successfully completed a critical fueling test of the Space Launch System rocket on Thursday evening at Kennedy Space Center in Florida.

The announcement followed a press conference in which Lori Glaze, NASA's Moon to Mars program manager, confirmed that the wet dress rehearsal — a full simulation of launch-day fueling and countdown operations — had gone as planned. "Following that successful wet dress yesterday, we're now targeting March 6 as our earliest launch attempt," Glaze said, while cautioning that pad work, data analysis, and a flight readiness review still need to be completed.

item.title: Artemis II launch set for March 6 after fueling test successful
item.description:
NASA is targeting March 6 as the launch date for its Artemis II mission after engineers successfully completed a critical fueling test of the Space Launch System rocket on the evening of February 19, overcoming hydrogen leak problems that had derailed an earlier attempt and delayed the historic crewed journey to the moon.

The four-member crew — Commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, mission specialists Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen — began preparing to enter a roughly 14-day quarantine on February 20 in Houston, a step NASA said would "preserve flexibility in the March launch window."

item.title: Indie game publisher says TikTok ran racist AI ads without its consent
item.description:
Finji, the independent game studio behind Night in the Woods and Tunic, has accused TikTok of using generative AI to alter its advertisements without permission, including one that introduced a racist, sexualized stereotype of one of the studio's characters. TikTok declined to comment on the record when contacted by IGN, which first reported the story.

The dispute centers on ads Finji runs through TikTok for its games, including the upcoming title Usual June. According to Finji CEO and co-founder Rebekah Saltsman, the studio's TikTok ad account has all AI features disabled, yet AI-modified versions of its ads have been appearing on the platform as if posted directly from Finji's official account.

item.title: Up to 20,000 unaccounted for after ISIS camp empties in Syria
item.description: U.S. intelligence agencies have concluded that between 15,000 and 20,000 individuals, including affiliates of the Islamic State, are now unaccounted for following a mass departure from Syria's al-Hol detention camp, according to a report by The Wall Street Journal citing U.S. officials familiar with the assessment. The finding underscores what analysts and Western diplomats have described as one of the most acute counterterrorism failures since the fall of ISIS's self-declared caliphate in 2019.

item.title: EU fails to agree on new Russia sanctions package ahead of war anniversary
item.description:
EU ambassadors failed to reach agreement on the bloc's 20th package of sanctions against Russia on Friday, with a proposed ban on maritime services for Russian oil tankers remaining the central obstacle as the fourth anniversary of Moscow's full-scale invasion of Ukraine approaches on February 24.

EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas expressed confidence the package would still be adopted, telling reporters, "Next Monday, we aim to adopt the 20th sanctions package against Russia". Negotiations among ambassadors are expected to continue over the weekend before foreign ministers meet in Brussels on February 23.

item.title: Trump orders new 10% global tariff hours after Supreme Court strikes down IEEPA levies
item.description:
President Trump appeared in the White House briefing room on Friday afternoon flanked by Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Attorney General Pam Bondi, and U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer to deliver a defiant response to the Supreme Court's 6-3 ruling that his sweeping tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act were unlawful. Trump called the decision "deeply disappointing" and announced he would immediately sign an executive order imposing a new 10% global tariff under Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974, "over and above our normal tariffs already being charged".

The announcement marks the administration's first concrete step in a contingency plan developed over months in anticipation of a possible court defeat.

item.title: UK considers removing Andrew from royal succession
item.description:
The UK government is considering legislation to remove Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor from the royal line of succession, the BBC reported on Friday, a day after the former prince became the first senior royal in modern history to be arrested. The move marks a reversal from the government's position in October 2025, when Downing Street said there were "no plans" for legislative changes to the succession order.

Andrew, 66, was arrested at Wood Farm on the King's Sandringham estate on Thursday morning — his birthday — on suspicion of misconduct in public office. Thames Valley Police said he was detained as part of an investigation into allegations that he shared confidential government information with convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein while serving as the UK's special trade envoy. He was held for approximately 11 hours at Aylsham police station in Norfolk before being released under investigation.

item.title: NOAA adopts new El Nino index as warming outpaces old system
item.description: The natural El Nino cycle that shapes weather patterns around the globe is both amplifying and being reshaped by a rapidly warming planet, prompting U.S. forecasters to adopt a new measurement system and researchers to trace how the interplay between these forces helped drive recent record temperatures.

item.title: Germany's Merz to visit China for first talks with Xi since taking office
item.description: Chancellor Friedrich Merz will depart Berlin on Tuesday for his first official visit to China, where he will meet with President Xi Jinping and Premier Li Qiang in what German officials described as an effort to find "the right balance of cooperation" between Europe's largest economy and its biggest trading partner.

item.title: New studies bolster theory that viruses sparked complex life
item.description: A pair of recent studies is reviving a long-debated question in evolutionary biology: did viruses help give rise to all complex life on Earth? The discovery of a new giant virus in Japan and fresh genomic evidence that ancient microbes could tolerate oxygen are together lending new weight to the idea that the cell nucleus — the defining feature of plants, animals, and fungi — may trace its origins to a viral infection billions of years ago.

item.title: New battery designs tackle fire risk and scarce metals
item.description: A flurry of new studies published this week from laboratories in China, Hong Kong, and the United States detail battery designs built around safer electrolytes and more durable materials, offering a glimpse of energy storage systems that could move beyond the flammability and resource constraints of conventional lithium-ion technology.
